newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open sharply lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious were called to open sharply lower Monday as the New York gold market was expected to tumble to move in line with the sharp losses in London Friday and Monday, dealers said.
New York metals futures markets reopened Monday after U.S. Independence Day holiday Friday.
COMEX August gold was called to open $7.00 to $8.00 lower from Thursday's close of $325.20 an ounce, a 12-year low.
London bullion was fixed this morning at $318.75, down from $324.45 Friday afternoon.
Gold has lost 13 percent of its value so far this year as central banks reviewed the worth of holding reserves. Last Thursday, Reserve Bank of Australia said it sold most of its reserves.
Bearish sentiment was still flushing out investors from the yellow metal market, dealers said.
On ACCESS, August COMEX gold was down $8.20 at $317.00, traded $325.80 to $315.50.
The tumble in gold was expected to drag down the rest of the precious metals complex, traders said.
COMEX September silver was called to open 4.0 to 6.0 cents lower. On ACCESS, September was off 6.5 cents at $4.505.
NYMEX October platinum was called down $5.00 to $6.00, with NYMEX September palladium called off $0.50 to $1.00.

Russia's state precious metals export agency, Almazjuvelirexport, will resume exports of platinum group metals this month, the Itar-Tass news agency quoted a Finance Ministry official as saying Monday.
Japanese traders said last week that the agency had said long-delayed export shipments would resume around July 10.
